narrative.overview:
Schleifpunkt is the category standard executed cleanly: a German tool-and-DIY webshop in the lineage of Contorion and the Festool online shop. White pages, a warm light-grey well behind every product photo, hairline borders, and the logo's deep green on every primary action and active state. Renting a machine works like buying a product: same card, same grid, same cart. The visitor should recognise the shop's mechanics on sight and spend their attention on machines, prices and dates.

Density is retail-normal: four-up product grids on wide screens, 44px controls, compact meta lines, prices set bold with tabular figures. Depth is almost flat. Hairlines and the grey well do the structural work; a soft shadow appears only when a card is hovered or when something floats (suggestions dropdown, mobile drawer). One family, Sofia Sans, carries everything from the 800-weight hero headline to the 0.8rem category line.

Convention is the commitment. A themed, decorative direction was rejected by the user in favour of a normal webshop, so the system has no signature quirk to protect; its rules exist to keep it ordinary, legible and fast to scan.
keyCharacteristics: White pages, warm grey (#f5f5f2) image tiles and summary panels, hairline borders.
Logo green for primary actions, active navigation, current page and focus.
Signal yellow is rationed to three jobs: the hero CTA, the "Miete" badge, the cart count.
One sans family in 400 to 800; tabular numerals on every price, count and date.
Flat at rest; shadows only on hover and on floating layers.

rules.name: The Three Yellow Jobs Rule
rules.body: Signal yellow appears in exactly three places: the single hero CTA, the "Miete" rental badge, and the cart count. It never fills a second button on the same screen, never marks a sale, never becomes a section background. If a new element wants yellow, it should be green.

rules.name: The Green Means Go Rule
rules.body: Every primary action, every "you are here" marker and every focus ring is logo green. Green is not decoration; do not use it for large fills except the 36px service strip.

rules.name: The Ink On Yellow Rule
rules.body: Text on yellow is always ink (#1b1f1c), never white.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every price, count, date and page number uses tabular lining figures (the `.tabular` utility), so columns of prices align.

rules.name: The Weight Not Face Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from weight and size in Sofia Sans. No second display face, no italics for emphasis, no letter-spaced uppercase labels above headings.

rules.name: The Familiar Grid Rule
rules.body: Product collections are always a uniform card grid of 2, 3 or 4 columns. No bento layouts, featured oversize tiles or carousels in place of a listing.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page carries a shadow at rest. Cards gain the hover lift; dropdowns and drawers carry theirs because they float. No hard offset shadows.

dos: **Do** use logo green for every primary action, active marker, current page and focus ring.
**Do** keep yellow to its three jobs: the hero CTA, the "Miete" badge and the cart count, always with ink text.
**Do** put product photos in the warm-grey well (#f5f5f2) with multiply blending and contained fit.
**Do** lay product collections out as 2 / 3 / 4-column card grids inside the 1320px container, paginated at 20.
**Do** set prices, counts, dates and page numbers in tabular figures, with units in smaller muted text.
**Do** use 8px radius for cards and panels, 6px for controls, 4px for badges.
**Do** keep surfaces flat at rest; use the hover lift on cards and the floating shadow only for dropdowns and drawers.
donts: **Don't** use yellow for a second button, a sale marker, a section background or decorative highlights.
**Don't** add a second typeface, decorative display type, or letter-spaced uppercase labels above headings.
**Don't** reintroduce themed or ornamental treatments (textures, enamel plates, stamps, illustrated frames); the user chose a conventional shop over a themed one.
**Don't** use hard offset shadows or shadows on resting cards.
**Don't** replace listings with carousels, bento grids or oversized featured tiles.
**Don't** put white text on yellow or on the pale tints.
